x-handover.name: screening results
x-handover.source: Anil Wipat, bioprospecting use case slides, dbtl-synbio/dbtlhub, 10 Nov 2026
x-handover.note: The use case numbers its handovers. Carrying that number in the contract means two teams arguing about 'the Design handover' are provably arguing about the same one.

title: Test -> Learn handover (generic)
description: The handover the flash deck calls 'peak area is not flux'. The common ground: every result resolves to a Design item, every number carries unit and method, and the profile declares what Learn cannot work without - a blank-corrected signal for bioprospecting, a titre normalised per gDW with declared uncertainty for biomanufacturing.

build_ref.description: The chain back to Build, and through it to Design. Without this a measurement cannot be traced to what was built.

normalised_to.description: The basis a derived value is expressed per, e.g. 'gDW'. Required by profiles whose Learn step needs a rate rather than a raw signal.

reads.description: Crates or packages this handover READ but did not produce. Information in this framework normally flows one way, from the phase that made something to the phase that receives it. This is the other direction: a receiving phase states what it can do, and the sending phase has to have looked. Referenced, never inlined - the package stays small and the graph joins the crates by their identifiers.

role.description: constraints: limits this package had to respect. context: read to interpret something. upstream: where the material came from.

checksum.description: Which version was read. A shared crate grows between rounds, so 'the Build crate' is not a unique thing to have read.

limits.description: Limits this package was built to respect, lifted out of the crates named in 'reads'. Carried here rather than left in the crate so that a check can compare against them, and 'from' says which crate each one came out of. A limit is not a use-case constant and does not belong in the profile: it is this run's equipment and this round's budget, and it changes between rounds.

from.description: The crate this limit was read out of.

stated_by.description: Who or what put it there - a researcher seeding the crate before round 1, or a phase recording its own equipment.

crate.description: The run's crate, as it stands when this handover is made. Carried so the checks below can read what Test recorded about each reading - the three things a table of numbers cannot say about itself.

x-dbtl-checks.message: the profile requires this measurement before Learn can use the data
x-dbtl-checks.fix_hint: not auto-fixable: a measurement that was never taken cannot be supplied. Either the instrument output is found, or the sample is reported as incomplete

x-dbtl-checks.message: the profile requires this on a reading before a model is fitted to it
x-dbtl-checks.fix_hint: not auto-fixable: whether the blank was subtracted, how many replicates there were and whether the value sat inside the instrument's range are facts about the run. An agent that supplied them would be inventing the conditions of an experiment
